title: VoiceStudio: the free, local ElevenLabs alternative
notes: Facts checked 2026-10-04: github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio (README, LICENSE-NOTICE.md, docs/feature-catalog.md, docs/mcp.md; created 2026-04-09, 52,915 stars, +16,775 in the trending week), k2-fsa/OmniVoice (README, docs/languages.md: 646 languages, 581,489 h, English 206,061 h, median 10.2 h; 3-10 s reference clip; CC-BY-NC weights), elevenlabs.io/pricing (Pro $99/month = 600,000 credits, about 600 minutes), Hugging Face model cards (CosyVoice 3: Apache-2.0). The narration is Chatterbox (MIT), made on the CPU of a laptop without a discrete GPU.

lines.text: Ten hours of AI voice a month? On ElevenLabs, that's the $99 plan.
say: Ten hours of AI voice a month?
On Eleven Labs, that's the ninety-nine dollar plan.

lines.text: This app does it on your own computer. No meter, no subscription.
say: This app does it on your own computer.
No meter, no subscription.

lines.text: It's called VoiceStudio. It clones voices, designs new ones, and dubs videos into other languages.
say: It's called Voice Studio.
It clones voices, designs new ones, and dubs videos into other languages.

lines.text: It's open source, not even six months old, and just passed 52,000 GitHub stars.
say: It's open source, not even six months old, and just passed fifty-two thousand GitHub stars.

lines.text: Nearly a third of them arrived in the last seven days.
say: Nearly a third of them arrived in the last seven days.

lines.text: So how does one free app replace a voice studio?
say: So how does one free app replace a voice studio?

lines.text: Think of it as a tape deck. The app is the deck. The voice models are the tapes.
say: Think of it as a tape deck.
The app is the deck.
The voice models are the tapes.

lines.text: There are more than a dozen. The default tape, OmniVoice, learned from 581,000 hours of speech.
say: There are more than a dozen.
The default tape, Omni Voice, learned from five hundred eighty-one thousand hours of speech.

lines.text: That's how it speaks 646 languages. But look at the split.
say: That's how it speaks six hundred forty-six languages.
But look at the split.

lines.text: English got over 200,000 hours. Half the languages got about ten each.
say: English got over two hundred thousand hours.
Half the languages got about ten each.

lines.text: To copy a voice, it needs a clip of just three to ten seconds.
say: To copy a voice, it needs a clip of just three to ten seconds.

lines.text: No clip? Describe one: age, pitch, accent, even a whisper, and it designs the voice.
say: No clip?
Describe one: age, pitch, accent, even a whisper, and it designs the voice.

lines.text: Dubbing chains it all: transcribe the video, translate it, re-voice each speaker in time.
say: Dubbing chains it all: transcribe the video, translate it, re-voice each speaker in time.

lines.text: It even runs a local server, so your AI agents can speak too.
say: It even runs a local server, so your AI agents can speak too.

lines.text: Nvidia, Apple Silicon, or a plain laptop: it runs on all three, just slower without a graphics card.
say: Nvidia, Apple Silicon, or a plain laptop: it runs on all three, just slower without a graphics card.

lines.text: Now the catch. The app is free, but the default voice model's licence is non-commercial.

lines.text: Making money? Swap in an Apache-licensed tape, like CosyVoice. And only clone voices you have permission to use.

lines.text: One more thing. This narration is AI too, made free on a laptop with no graphics card.

lines.text: That's today's tool. There's a new one every day.
